ranking.rationale: A small slot shift keeps the arrival stream regular and removes this aircraft from the taxiway peak, with taxi_congestion=0.62 being the main concern.
A small slot shift disturbs sector flow least and avoids adding taxi movements at the congested peak.
Larger slot shift still avoids airborne holding and taxi additions, though it moves the stream more than a 15-minute shift.
Moves the flight off the destination peak without holding, but a 30-minute shift disturbs the stream more than smaller shifts.
Ground hold at origin keeps aircraft off destination taxiways and avoids airborne holding, but adds 25 minutes of delay upstream.
Adds a short extra taxi, which slightly increases taxiway load under taxi_congestion=0.62, but the added taxi time is small.
Adds 5 minutes of extra taxi into a congested taxiway environment, which works against my taxiway goal.
Airborne hold feeds aircraft into the arrival peak and disturbs sector throughput more than slot or ground options.
Longer airborne hold adds more traffic to the destination arrival window and is the weaker choice for wake spacing and sector flow.
Diversion removes the flight from the destination arrival stream entirely and is the most disruptive option to sector throughput.
Diversion is the most disruptive option to sector throughput and gives the largest delay estimate.

Earlier arrival with no added airborne time protects the estimated connection and keeps crew_duty_remaining_min from eroding.
Earliest arrival option with no added airborne time; best for the connection and duty day, though its estimate is the same as SLOT-15's.
Only 2 minutes of extra taxi, no airborne time; minor added delay on the ground.
Extra taxi of 5 minutes is acceptable on the ground but costs more time than GATE_A12.
Later arrival with no airborne time, but it erodes the estimated connection and crew duty.
Largest ground-side delay of the slot options; risks the estimated connection and duty day.
Airborne holding draws on fuel_reserve_min (estimated) and occurs in weather given WEATHER_DELAY present; tolerable only if ground options fail.

Avoids the weather but adds a second approach, loses the connection, and adds about 80.6 minutes; last resort only.
Farther alternate than CSG, loses the connection and adds the longest delay of the diversions; last resort only.

Larger earlier shift further clears the disrupted hour and taxi peak, at a somewhat larger stream disturbance.
Later shift adds some spacing margin but places the flight nearer the disrupted hour than an earlier slot would.
Later shift of 30 minutes keeps the flight in the disrupted period longer, a weaker wake-spacing and peak position.
Holds the aircraft at origin, keeping it off the taxiways and out of the destination peak without airborne holding.
Adds a small amount of taxi time while taxi_congestion is high, which is a mild cost to the taxiway goal.
Longer taxi routing adds more taxiway occupancy while taxi_congestion is high; accepted only as the least harmful airborne-free concession.
Airborne holding adds aircraft into the disrupted destination peak, against the wake-spacing priority.

ranking.rationale: A ground hold at origin keeps the crew off airborne holding during flight.WEATHER_DELAY=247 and adds no airborne fuel draw on fuel_reserve_min=103.8 (estimated).

Modest later shift; tolerable but worse than earlier slots for connections and duty.
Adds 20 minutes airborne in weather exposure draw on fuel_reserve_min=103.8 (estimated); tolerable only as a fallback.

Avoids weather but adds a second approach and loses all connections; nearest alternate is preferred among diversions.
